Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.texteditor

Class SyntaxHighlighter

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.texteditor.SyntaxHighlighter
public final class SyntaxHighlighter extends Object
The Advanced Text Editor's syntax colouriser: a small, dependency-free scanner that turns text into SyntaxHighlighter.Tokens according to a declarative Language, plus a batch applier that paints those tokens onto a StyledDocument with an EditorTheme's colours.

The scanner is a single forward pass — comments, strings, numbers, directives, markup tags and keywords — with adjacent plain runs merged so the token list stays proportional to the interesting content, not to the whitespace. It never throws on malformed input: an unterminated comment or string simply extends to the end of the text, which is what a live editor wants while the user is still typing.

tokenize(java.lang.String, org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.texteditor.Language) is pure (safe off the EDT, unit-testable headless); apply(javax.swing.text.StyledDocument, org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.texteditor.Language, org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.texteditor.EditorTheme) is the only Swing-facing half and mutates the document in one batch under no locks of its own, so callers invoke it on the EDT.

    • tokenize

      public static List<SyntaxHighlighter.Token> tokenize(String text, Language lang)
      Scans text into a merged, non-overlapping token list covering the whole input. A null language behaves like Languages.PLAIN.

    • apply

      public static void apply(StyledDocument doc, Language lang, EditorTheme theme)
      Paints the whole document in one batch: every character first gets the theme's plain style, then each non-plain token overrides its span. No-op for documents above MAX_HIGHLIGHT_CHARS (callers show them uncolourised) and for Languages.PLAIN.
